back: Single instruction, single data: one processing unit, one instruction at a time on one data item.
Single instruction, multiple data: one instruction applied to many data items; used by graphics processors.
Multiple instruction, single data: rare; used where several units process the same data and results are compared.
Multiple instruction, multiple data: several processors run different instructions on different data; multi-core PCs and clusters.
Shared: one common memory, can bottleneck. Distributed: each processor has its own memory and messages are sent.
Speed-up = 1 ÷ ((1 − p) + p ÷ n), where p is the parallel fraction.
1 ÷ (1 − p): the sequential part sets the limit.
Large problems split into independent parts with little communication, such as weather forecasting and simulation.
